claims.text: High-temperature oxidation of additive-manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 causes significant elemental redistribution within its nanoprecipitates.
Atom Probe Tomography can reveal the proposed oxidation-induced redistribution in the nanoprecipitates.
Nanoprecipitate elemental redistribution correlates with changes in oxide-scale formation.
Nanoprecipitate elemental redistribution correlates with changes in oxide-scale adherence.
The additive-manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy contains dual nanoprecipitates.
The as-fabricated alloy has a well-defined nanoscale structure.
Oxidation temperatures of 700–1000 °C are representative of demanding gas-turbine, power-plant, or aerospace service.
The nanoprecipitates act as localized reservoirs for aluminum and titanium.
Compositional shifts in the nanoprecipitates mediate oxide-scale formation.
Compositional shifts in the nanoprecipitates mediate oxide-scale integrity.
Oxidation promotes selective elemental migration within the nanoprecipitates.
Redistribution of oxidation-resistant elements can reinforce formation of a protective oxide layer.
Localized depletion of oxidation-resistant elements can produce non-protective oxide scales.
Nanoprecipitate redistribution influences overall oxidation kinetics and degradation.
Post-oxidation APT will show measurable accumulation or depletion of oxide-forming elements within nanoprecipitates.
The measured compositional changes will correlate with oxide-scale morphology and protective performance.
Cast and wrought counterparts do not exhibit the same nanoprecipitate refinement as the additive-manufactured alloy.
The additive-manufactured alloy exhibits oxidation-behavior enhancements relative to cast and wrought counterparts.
APT can resolve nanoscale elemental redistribution in this oxidized alloy.

contradictions.description: The baseline states that additive manufacturing produces oxidation-behavior enhancements relative to cast and wrought material, while the mechanism allows redistribution to produce either protective or non-protective scales and the uncertainty field says the redistribution–oxidation relationship remains undetermined.
